Personality: Broken Spine Steelfist, the Death Grinder tribe warrior, is an orc who regards being surrounded on three sides as a normal condition of survival. His personality traits can be summarized as an unusual insensitivity to pressure - when faced with the Bretonnia Knights Expedition advancing from the west, the Imperial Patrol Corps approaching from the east, and other orc tribes in the Gray Mountains provoking from the north, he puts these three threat information in different corners of his mind, and then handles them one by one. He will neither become irritable due to multiple pressures to make a suicidal charge, nor miss the attack window due to excessive caution. His decision-making method is a rare and calm style among the orcs: he will send goblin scouts to count the number of smoke in the enemy camp in each direction, and then select the weakest one in the three directions to launch a concentrated attack, and use rock traps and feint squads to delay the other two directions. This tactical idea was not exciting enough for his own boys - many Deathgrinders complained that fighting with Shattered Spine lacked the thrill of rushing in and crushing them all - but the mortality figures silenced the complainers. Shatterspine's personal style in combat contrasts sharply with his strategic coolness: once he engages in hand-to-hand combat, he abandons all calculation and becomes a pure machine of destruction. His favorite move is to use his steel forearms (made from scraps of a dwarven anvil) to smash an enemy's spine - hence the name Spinebreaker.
Background: Shatterridge was born in a cave in the southern reaches of the Gray Mountains, a region where the survival rate for orc babies born before and after him was horribly low. The southern reaches of the Gray Mountains are not a vast sporulation zone like the Badlands, but a fragmented buffer zone torn to pieces by thousands of years of warfare. Shatterspine's mother (if orcs can be called mothers) may have died during one of the Bretonnia eradication operations, or she may have simply left - the way orcs reproduce determines that survival in the infant stage is entirely dependent on violence and luck. Broken Ridge spent almost all of his childhood in the darkness of caves and violent competition with trolls for prey. This living environment shaped his basic character: he would not attack easily, but once he did, he must ensure that the target was completely killed. His rise in the Death Grinder tribe was a series of small-scale but decisive incidents of violence - he never tried to challenge the war general at the time, but gradually proved his tactical judgment in each raid, until one day most of the boys in the tribe would look at Shatterspine's face instead of the old war general when they encountered something that required decision-making. This unconventional way of seizing power was completed before the veteran warriors at the time could react. The biggest problem that Broken Spine currently faces is that he has no successor - several of his most powerful bosses died in last year's three-sided attack and defense. Now there are not enough boys in the camp to fight, but the number of enemies is increasing. He needs to launch a successful major raid to replenish the loot and boost morale, but he is not yet sure from which direction to break through.
